clue.text: Gambling theorist?

parts.note: one who gambles on shares and one who forms theories are both described by the same word, so a gambling theorist is a pun on its two senses

explanation.surface: A thinker who has worked out a system for beating the bookies.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a person who trades riskily for profit and a person who forms theories; the question mark flags the play on both.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who buys shares hoping for a rise is gambling, and someone who conjectures is a theorist; one word covers both.

clue.text: Southern tree belt

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree in the south of the country forms a belt across the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Would he be a nobleman in New.York? Not quite

definitions.text: Would he be a nobleman in New.York? Not quite

parts.words: Would he be a nobleman in New.York? Not quite
parts.note: a common American first name is also a British rank of peer, so a New Yorker bearing it carries the title but is not really a nobleman

explanation.surface: Is a man of this name a nobleman in New York? Not really.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a rank in the British peerage and an ordinary American first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of British peer just below marquess is also a familiar first name in the USA.

clue.text: I'm blue 'with angina — to move would be unthinkable

indicators.note: to move means these letters are to be shifted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of I'm blue are part of the fodder
the letters of angina are part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A depressed patient with chest pains finds moving inconceivable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' signals rearranging the letters of I'M BLUE and ANGINA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too strange to be imagined is inconceivable, a synonym of unthinkable.

clue.text: Grey like a chicken

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a hen is a female chicken

explanation.surface: Someone is pale-faced like a frightened chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale grey like ash describes a face drained of colour.

clue.text: Beetles encountered by mountaineers

explanation.surface: Insects met by climbers on the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetles looks like the insects, but here it is a verb: to beetle is to jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to project over something, as cliffs and brows do; and climbers meet jutting rock ledges on their routes.

clue.text: Turner gives back gratuities

indicators.note: gives back tells us the word for gratuities is to be read backwards

parts.note: gratuities are tips given for service

explanation.surface: A painter named Turner returns the money he was tipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but it is a thing that turns: the rotating rod meat is roasted on.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting rod that is rotated over a fire is something that turns, hence a turner.

clue.text: Long official notice about take off suited one, perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: Long official notice about take off suited one, perhaps (3-7): PIN-STRIPED is STRIP (take off) inside PINED, but PINED is 'longed', and no clue word as held accounts for the D: 'official notice' gives nothing that fits
annotationWithheld.clue: Long official notice about take off suited one, perhaps

clue.text: Dinners set out in the latest style

indicators.note: out means the letters are laid out afresh, put out of their original order

parts.note: the letters of dinners are part of the fodder
the letters of set are part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Dinner tables are laid out in the most fashionable manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as laying a table, but set is fodder and only 'out' signals the rearranging of DINNERS and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and up to date is the quality of following the latest style.

clue.text: Damascene street directions put in order

parts.note: the Bible names a street in Damascus called Straight (Acts 9:11)
E is east, a compass direction
N is north, another compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding a street in Damascus have been tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts, Saul is sent to 'the street which is called Straight' in Damascus, so a Damascene street is STRAIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy or arrange something neatly is a synonym of putting it in order.

clue.text: Performing notes not duplicated

parts.note: a performer on stage is said to be on
C is a musical note
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: A musician plays each passage only one time, never repeating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done a single time and not repeated has not been duplicated.

clue.text: Unusual African lions found in USA

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters of African are part of the fodder
the letters of lions are part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Strange: big cats from Africa turning up in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in USA' looks like a description of the lions, but it defines people from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a western US state are people found in America.

clue.text: Unlike Richard, not equipped for successful wooing

explanation.surface: A lover who is no Lionheart lacks what it takes to win a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard I of England was called the Lionheart; the second sense recalls the proverb 'faint heart never won fair lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard the Lionheart was famously brave, so his opposite is timid; and the proverb says a timid lover never wins a lady.

clue.text: Give name in before church order of seniority appears.

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to cede is to give up or yield
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clerk is told to give his name before the church's ranking is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'appears' are link words; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking by status or rank, who goes first at a ceremony, is precedence.

clue.text: Stress of being a teenager?

explanation.surface: The pressures of adolescence.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so a teenager is under a score; the question mark flags the punning second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise something is to underline it; and anyone aged under twenty is literally below a score of years.

clue.text: Interpretation giving the right impression about Newton

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right

indicators.note: about means the word for impression goes round the letter for Newton

parts.note: an impression is a print run of a book, an edition
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A performance gives the correct picture of the scientist Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton is not the scientist but the unit of force, abbreviated N.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a piece of music or a role is a performer's interpretation of it.

clue.text: It warns motorists of the turning. ahead

definitions.text: It warns motorists of the turning. ahead

parts.words: It warns motorists of the turning. ahead
parts.note: describes the flashing light on a car that tells drivers behind it is about to turn

explanation.surface: A road sign warns drivers of a junction coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a road sign, but it is the flashing light on the car itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's flashing signal lamp shows other drivers which way it is going to go.

clue.text: Crucifixion puts' an end to fiery revolutionary …

indicators.note: puts an end to says the letters sit at the very end of the word Crucifixion

explanation.surface: A crucifixion finally finishes off a blazing rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ixion was bound to a fiery wheel that turned for ever, so he is a fiery revolutionary in the sense of revolving.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king was punished on a burning wheel spinning eternally, making him one who revolves in flames.

clue.text: … and the French revolutionary leads a disciple

indicators.note: leads means the revolutionary goes in front of the French word for the

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary heads a band of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the clue before, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a chela is a pupil or follower of a guru, i.e. a disciple.

clue.text: Finds protection in Norfolk town

indicators.note: in means the word for protection is put inside the name of the town

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
cover is shelter or protection

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down shelter in a small town in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS is a small market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find, a straight synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Movement in simple dance, tempo initially

annotationWithheld.why: Movement in simple dance tempo initially (12): DISPLACEMENT is an anagram of SIMPLE DANCE + T, but the only anagram signal is Movement, which is also the definition, so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Movement in simple dance, tempo initially

clue.text: Unlucky French bather married a renegade

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or renegade

explanation.surface: An ill-fated Frenchman taking a bath wed a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The French revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The revolutionary leader was murdered while bathing, making him a famously unlucky French bather.

clue.text: Operatic heroine repeating note .

indicators.note: repeating means the musical note is written twice in a row

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soprano in an opera keeps singing the same note.
explanation.definitionFit: The consumptive seamstress in Puccini's La Bohème is a famous opera heroine.

clue.text: Hitch horse after finish of Oaks

indicators.note: after means the horse comes behind the final letter of Oaks
finish of means only the last letter of the word Oaks is taken

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: Harness a horse once the Oaks race is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a famous English horse race at Epsom, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected difficulty or obstacle is a hitch.

clue.text: Retreat despite lack ..of authorisation.

parts.note: no means none, a lack
an OK is permission or authorisation

explanation.surface: Troops withdraw even though they have not been given permission.
explanation.walkthrough: Retreat looks like a verb for troops pulling back, but it is a noun: a quiet corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded corner where one can hide away is a retreat.

clue.text: Outstanding tax return Number One is in for a food 'shortage

parts.note: an outstanding performer is a star; star as an adjective means outstanding
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

indicators.note: return means the abbreviation for number and the numeral for one are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unpaid tax return is filed and the top person is in line for a famine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NO + I into ION. The surface suggests an overdue tax return, but return applies to Number One.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme lack of food leading to hunger or death is starvation, a food shortage.

clue.text: Four fifths of prime number is divisible by two

indicators.note: four fifths of a five-letter word means one of its five letters is dropped, here the first

parts.note: seven is a prime number

explanation.surface: A mathematical fact: most of a prime can be split into two.
explanation.walkthrough: Four fifths of SEVEN drops its first letter, leaving four of the five.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number that halves exactly with no remainder is described as even.

clue.text: Demonstrating… in favour of examinations

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
testing is the setting of tests or examinations

explanation.surface: Students are on a march in support of exams.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests students marching in favour of exams; the definition is the marching itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to make a public objection, as demonstrators do.
